title: PeeringDB Plus - Service Overview
description: Comprehensive observability dashboard for PeeringDB Plus covering sync health, HTTP RED metrics, per-type sync detail, Go runtime, and business metrics.

list.expr: count by (service_version) (pdbplus_build_info{service_name="$service"}) unless count by (service_version) (pdbplus_build_info{service_name="$service"} offset 10m)
list.name: Deploys
list.textFormat: First report of a new version

list.name: Machine restarts
list.textFormat: The VM restarted (its fly_instance_cpu counters reset)

panels.title: Data Freshness
panels.description: Seconds since last successful sync. Green <1h healthy, yellow 1-2h delayed, red >2h indicates a problem.

panels.title: Sync Success Rate
panels.description: Share of sync attempts that succeeded over the dashboard time range. Should be near 100%. A failed attempt counts even when the retry 30s later passes. Drops indicate PeeringDB API issues or database write failures.

panels.title: Sync Duration (p95)
panels.description: 95th percentile sync cycle time over the attempts of the last hour, by mode (incremental or full), failed attempts included. Normal range is 30-120s depending on data volume and mode. A 1h window holds about 4 cycles at the 15m cadence; a shorter window is empty between cycles.

panels.title: Fallback Events
panels.description: Count of incremental-to-full sync fallbacks over the dashboard time range. Should be 0 under normal operation. Non-zero means incremental sync failed and a full re-fetch was triggered.

panels.title: Sync Operations
panels.description: Count of completed sync cycles by status (success/failed) per time bucket. Red bars are failures. If freshness is red, check here for errors.

panels.title: Role Transitions
panels.description: LiteFS primary/replica role transition events

panels.title: Request Rate by Route
panels.description: HTTP requests per second grouped by route. Health checks (/healthz, /readyz, gRPC health) are left out: they are about 90% of all requests and hide the other routes. Synthetic Monitoring probe requests (user_agent_synthetic_type="test") are left out too.

panels.title: Error Rate (5xx)
panels.description: Ratio of 5xx server errors to routed HTTP requests. It uses the request selector of the availability SLO (deploy/grafana/slos/), whose burn-rate rules alert on this ratio. Health probes and POST /sync are left out: a /readyz 503 is a readiness verdict, not a failed request. Requests with no http_route (404 scans, the readiness gate 503 before the first sync) and Synthetic Monitoring probe requests are left out too.

panels.title: Active Requests
panels.description: Currently in-flight HTTP requests

panels.title: Latency p50 / p95 / p99
panels.description: HTTP response-time percentiles (p50/p95/p99) across user-facing routes. Health/readiness probes are excluded: they are ~92% of requests and otherwise drag the tail down, masking real API latency. Synthetic Monitoring probe requests are excluded too: one small fast query that would pull the percentiles down.

panels.title: Sync Throughput by Type
panels.description: Per-type upsert rate during sync windows. Network (net) and NetworkIxLan (netixlan) are typically the largest and slowest.

panels.title: Objects Synced per Type
panels.description: Total objects upserted per type over the selected time range (follows the time picker; rounded to whole objects). In incremental mode this tracks upstream churn. Large counts are normal for types like netixlan (~100K+ objects).

panels.title: Cascaded Deletes per Type
panels.description: Rows per type that sync marks deleted itself. Only the netixlan cascade emits this. It marks the live connections of a network that PeeringDB deleted without a tombstone for them (pdb_rir_status, about 0.7 networks a day, after about 22:55 UTC). Tombstones that PeeringDB sends are in Objects Synced per Type. The first primary start on v1.28.2 shows about 260. For another large value, look at the 'cascaded network deletes to netixlans' log.

panels.title: Fetch / Upsert Errors
panels.description: Sync fetch-step errors (cursor read, PeeringDB request, scratch write) and database upsert errors by type

panels.title: Goroutines
panels.description: Live goroutine count. Sustained growth is a leak signal. One line per machine (process group and region).

panels.title: Heap Memory
panels.description: Go heap memory currently in use. One line per machine (process group and region).

panels.title: Allocation Rate
panels.description: Bytes allocated per second by the Go runtime. One line per machine (process group and region).

panels.title: GC Goal
panels.description: Target heap size for the Go garbage collector. One line per machine (process group and region).

panels.title: Total Objects
panels.description: Sum of all rows across 13 entity types. ~1.5M is the steady-state size. Reported by the primary only.

panels.title: Objects by Type
panels.description: Object count per PeeringDB type. Reported by the primary only.

panels.title: Object Counts Over Time
panels.description: PeeringDB object counts per type over time. Reported by the primary only.

panels.title: Peak Heap
panels.description: Sync-cycle peak HeapInuse on the primary. Threshold line at 400 MiB — sustained breach should re-open the incremental-sync evaluation (Fly 512 MB VM cap).

panels.title: Peak RSS
panels.description: Sync-cycle peak RSS on the primary (VmHWM from /proc/self/status, reset at the start of each cycle). Threshold line at 384 MiB.

panels.title: Live Heap by Instance
panels.description: Per-VM Go heap from go_memory_used_bytes (OTel runtime gauge). Plots all fleet machines (primary + replicas) in the asymmetric fleet.

panels.title: Response Heap Delta — p50/p95/p99 by endpoint
panels.description: Per-request Go HeapInuse delta on pdbcompat list handlers (/api/*) from pdbplus_response_heap_delta_bytes histogram. p50/p95/p99 quantiles over a 5-minute rolling window, grouped by endpoint. Shows 'No data' when there is no /api/ traffic in the selected window — the histogram is only observed on pdbcompat list requests, not on /healthz, /ui/, /rest/v1/, /graphql, or ConnectRPC.

panels.title: Replica Lag
panels.description: Seconds since each replica last received a frame (an LTX file or a heartbeat) from the LiteFS primary (litefs_lag_seconds). It stays near 0 between commits because the primary sends heartbeats. A rising line means that the replica lost its stream.

panels.title: LTX Apply Lag
panels.description: Time from the creation of the last LTX file that each replica applied to its apply (litefs_db_lag_seconds). LiteFS sets it at each apply, so it keeps its last value between commits. No value until the replica applies an LTX file after a restart.

panels.title: Transactions Behind Primary
panels.description: LiteFS transactions that each replica is behind the primary (litefs_db_txid). 0 when the replica is up to date. The nodes read their values up to one collection interval apart, so a commit can show as 1 or more for one interval.

panels.title: Primary Commits
panels.description: Database commits on the primary per interval (litefs_db_commit_count). A sync cycle commits more than once: the sync_status writes and the sync transaction. Replicas never commit, so this panel reads the primary only.

panels.title: Primary LTX Size (raw)
panels.description: litefs_db_ltx_bytes on the primary as LiteFS 0.5 sets it. A commit sets it to the size of the new LTX file. Each retention pass (once a minute) sets it to the size of the LTX files on disk. A large commit shows in both values. Do not use it as a disk-usage signal.

panels.title: Connected Replicas
panels.description: Replicas with an open LiteFS stream to the primary (litefs_subscriber_count). It equals the number of replica machines when every replica is connected.

panels.title: Upstream Requests by Status Class
panels.description: Requests to the PeeringDB API per window, by status class (2xx, 3xx, 4xx, 5xx, other, network_error). Sync, FK backfill, netixlan cascade verification and the history sweep share one rate limiter. 4xx includes 429 rate limits and 403 WAF blocks; each is also logged as a WARN.

panels.title: Upstream Retries by Cause
panels.description: Retries of PeeringDB requests by cause: 429 (after the Retry-After delay) and 5xx. Empty when no request was retried.

panels.title: Rate-Limit Wait (p95)
panels.description: 95th percentile time that a PeeringDB request waited for the local rate limiter (PDBPLUS_PEERINGDB_RPS, burst 1). Waits of seconds are normal during a sync cycle; the limiter keeps requests under the upstream quota.

panels.title: History Sweep Requests
panels.description: Tombstone history sweep windows per type and result (ok, rate_limited, error). An incremental cycle sends up to PDBPLUS_HISTORY_MAX_REQUESTS_PER_CYCLE windows. ok counts a fetched window even when the cycle fails later and rolls back, so a type that repeats ok without moving on points at a failure after the fetch (see Sync Operations).

panels.title: FK Backfill
panels.description: Backfill attempts for missing FK parents, by parent type and result (hit, miss, ratelimited, error, deadline_exceeded). PDBPLUS_FK_BACKFILL_MAX_REQUESTS_PER_CYCLE caps the requests per cycle.

panels.title: FK Orphans
panels.description: Rows whose FK parent was still missing after backfill, by child type, parent type and action (drop: row skipped; null: optional FK set to NULL). The per-cycle WARN "fk orphans summary" has the detail.

panels.title: Probe Success by Location
panels.description: Share of the executions of the Synthetic Monitoring check peeringdb-plus-api (GET /api/net?asn=15169 through the public hostname) that passed in the last 15 minutes, by probe location. The check runs every 5 minutes, so the window holds 3 executions. The alert PdbPlusProbeFailing fires when 2 or more locations are below 50% for 5 minutes. Settings: deploy/grafana/synthetics/README.md.

panels.title: Probe Duration by Location
panels.description: Total time of the last execution of the Synthetic Monitoring check peeringdb-plus-api, by probe location: DNS, connect, TLS and the response through the Fly edge and proxy. The server time of the same request is a few milliseconds (HTTP RED Metrics row); the rest is the network path from the probe. max by (probe) joins the series of each check version (config_version label).

panels.title: CPU Throttled
panels.description: Share of time that the cgroup of each machine was throttled after it used its CPU quota (Fly.io metric fly_instance_cpu_throttle: the throttled_time of the cgroup cpu.stat, in centiseconds). A shared-CPU machine runs at a baseline (1/16 of a vCPU on a replica, 1/8 on the primary) and bursts above it from a balance; with no balance left, the kernel throttles it. The alert PdbPlusMachineCPUThrottled fires above 1% for 15 minutes. Needs the fly.io data source.

panels.title: CPU Use vs Baseline
panels.description: CPU time that each machine used, as a share of its baseline quota (fly_instance_cpu without the idle, iowait, steal and guest modes, divided by fly_instance_cpu_baseline). Above 100% the machine spends its burst balance (CPU Burst Balance panel). Needs the fly.io data source.

panels.title: CPU Burst Balance
panels.description: Burst balance of each machine, in seconds of CPU time (fly_instance_cpu_balance, in centiseconds). A machine adds to the balance while it uses less than its baseline and spends it above the baseline. At 0 it runs at the baseline and the kernel throttles it (CPU Throttled panel). Needs the fly.io data source.

panels.title: VM Memory Available
panels.description: MemAvailable of the VM of each machine (fly_instance_memory_mem_available): the memory that the kernel can give to processes, for the whole VM, that is the app, LiteFS and the page cache. The Go memory panels see the app only. A replica has 256 MB and the primary 512 MB. Near 0 the kernel stops the largest process (alert PdbPlusMachineOOMKilled). Needs the fly.io data source.

panels.title: Edge Error Responses
panels.description: Responses with a status of 400 or higher at the Fly.io edge, by status code (fly_edge_http_responses_count). The edge counts every request from the internet, including the Synthetic Monitoring probes, and also the 502 and 503 responses that the Fly proxy sends when it cannot reach a machine. The HTTP metrics of the app do not see those. Needs the fly.io data source.

panels.title: Edge Response Time p95
panels.description: 95th percentile response time that the Fly.io edge measures, by the region of the edge where the request entered the Fly network (fly_edge_http_response_time_seconds), for all requests including the Synthetic Monitoring probes. The server time of the app is in the Latency panel; the difference is the path from the edge to the machine. Needs the fly.io data source.
